summary: A target-level plan of the real weight-two Noether–Lefschetz interfaces required by the accepted Benoist route. It extends the common variation carrier by a compatible real action, separates geometric from coefficient conjugation, and supplies transported-class loci, Kodaira–Spencer contraction, the Griffiths formula, normal-boundary factorization, Green's criterion over the reals, componentwise genericity, lattice cosets, the Voisin pushforward-kernel cone, ordinary integral weak Lefschetz and the affine CW bound. Global geometric typing and several general proof suppliers remain explicit gaps; no implementation or formal closure is claimed.

nodes.title: Compatible real action on a weight-two variation
nodes.statement: On the imported finite-rank effective rational weight-two variation H over a smooth complex base with antiholomorphic involution c, a compatible real action is a rational local-system involution σ_b:H_Q,b→H_Q,c(b), with σ_c(b)σ_b=id, whose complex-linear extension exchanges H^(p,2-p)_b with H^(2-p,p)_c(b). Equivalently the semilinear composite τ_b=σ_C,b∘κ_b preserves Hodge types, where κ is coefficient conjugation. A flat G-stable chart identifies this data with an involutive real-linear σ on V=H_R,b and native fibre Hodge structures on C tensor_R V; it is only the action extension, not another VHS carrier.
hypotheses: H is the common rational VHS of ShimuraData:D3, of weight 2 and effective in the sense of the native predicate HodgeStructureOn.IsEffective on each fibre. In the source the base is B(C) for a smooth algebraic variety B over R and c is its antiholomorphic involution; the definition uses only a complex manifold with an antiholomorphic involution.
κ is the native conjugation; σ is geometric pullback, extended linearly in complex coefficients.
proofSteps: Attach the rational involution to the existing local system and require its square and compatibility with transport.
Use native conj_piece to compare the type-exchange condition for σ_C with type preservation for σ_Cκ.
In a G-stable marking transport σ_b to one fixed real fibre; do not turn a choice of marking into global triviality.

sources.locator: §1.1, p.1050 (the action (1.1) and the Tate convention); equation (1.3), §1.4, p.1052 (its two factors)
sources.match: The source lets G act on the rational local system over the base involution, extends it to the complexified fibres by the action on the local system tensored with complex conjugation, and assumes that this antilinear action preserves the Hodge pieces; (1.3) writes it as coefficient conjugation followed by the complex-linear geometric map.

acceptance: A real structure acts between fibres b and c(b), not inside every non-real fibre.
Separate σ_C from τ even at a fixed basepoint.

nodes.title: Geometric real weight-two variation
nodes.statement: If π:X→B is a smooth projective morphism of smooth algebraic varieties over R with surface fibres, the local system R²π_*Q on B(C), its Gauss–Manin bundle and Hodge filtration supplied by H.2 form an effective rational weight-two VHS with the compatible real action of real-action. Fibre H¹(Ω¹) identifies with H^(1,1), H²(O) with H^(0,2), and geometric conjugation sends the former Hodge type to its exchanged type at c(b). Torsion is removed only for the VHS lattice, H²(Z)/tors; ordinary integral topology below retains torsion.
hypotheses: π is smooth and projective; X and B are smooth over R.
Use the actual Betti/de Rham and coherent Hodge comparison, not an arbitrary chosen decomposition.
The identification of H¹(Ω¹) with H^(1,1) and of H²(O) with H^(0,2) is the one H.2/geometric-pure constructs; ComplexComparisonPartII:C1 is cited for the coherent cohomology of the fibres only.
proofSteps: Import the geometric pure variation and Gauss–Manin connection of H.2.
Pull back differential forms by the antiholomorphic geometric involution; it interchanges their holomorphic and antiholomorphic degrees.
Coefficient conjugation interchanges the degrees independently; conclude compatibility via combined-type.

nodes.title: Transported Hodge-class locus
nodes.statement: In a flat marking on a connected simply connected analytic open Δ at b₀, and for λ∈H_R,b₀, define NL_Δ(λ)={b∈Δ | transported λ lies in H_b^(1,1)}. Equivalently for real λ, it lies in F¹_b. The real locus is NL_Δ(λ)∩B(R), and for the real theorem λ is in V(1)^G. A non-simply-connected base uses the class on a chosen local-system branch; no globally preferred transport is asserted.
hypotheses: Δ is a flat trivializing chart; transport is the imported local-system identification.
The fibre structures are effective of weight2 and λ is real; the F¹ equivalence requires reality.
proofSteps: Use the native piece1 submodule for the marked fibre and take membership of 1 tensor λ.
For a real vector, coefficient conjugation fixes it, so membership in F¹ also implies membership in its conjugate.
Restrict to fixed basepoints only when asking for real deformations.

The positive sign belongs to differentiation of the moving filtration; the negative sign belongs to the quotient of a fixed flat class.

The fixed class obstruction in this quotient frame is -A(b)λ.
Differentiate and import derivative-connection; a moving quotient frame adds no term at a zero.

nodes.title: Griffiths derivative equals contraction
nodes.statement: Let π:X→B be a smooth projective morphism of smooth complex algebraic varieties with surface fibres, and H the geometric weight-two variation of H.2/geometric-pure on R²π_*Q with its Gauss–Manin connection. Under the natural identifications H_b^(1,1)≅H¹(X_b,Ω¹) and H_b^(0,2)≅H²(X_b,O), θ_b(v)(λ)=φ_λ(v) for every v∈T_bB and λ∈H_b^(1,1), where θ_b is the H.3 period symbol at p=1 restricted to H_b^(1,1) and φ_λ(v)=KS_b(v)∪λ. The equality has positive sign in the H.3 convention; the separate flat-class obstruction has negative sign. No real structure enters: geometric-real-variation uses the formula after complexifying a real family.
hypotheses: π is smooth projective over C with surface fibres, B smooth; use the natural coherent Hodge and de Rham/Betti comparisons.

The identifications of H^(1,1) with H¹(Ω¹) and of H^(0,2) with H²(O) are those of H.2/geometric-pure: the graded pieces of the de Rham filtration are the Hodge cohomology groups. The engine behind them (degeneration and the cohomological Hodge decomposition) is gap G9 of that packet and is recorded here in G1; coherent analytic cohomology alone does not give it.
The source proves the formula for any analytic family of compact Kähler manifolds and any degree; only weight two on surfaces is used here.
proofSteps: Choose local family coordinates; derivatives of transition maps give the Čech KS cocycle.
Differentiate a representative (1,1)-form: the component lowering holomorphic degree is contraction with that cocycle.
The remaining components lie in F¹ and disappear in H_C/F¹; identify the remaining class by Griffiths Proposition(1.20).

sources.match: The full local differential-form calculation identifies the period derivative with KS cup product.
This formula converts the contraction rank calculation into the variation derivative required by Green.

acceptance: Comparison uses the actual geometric KS map; a declared linear map of the right type is insufficient.

nodes.title: Normal-boundary factorization of divisor contraction
nodes.statement: Let C⊂T⊂X be smooth projective complex varieties of dimensions 1, 2, 3, so that C is an effective Cartier divisor on T and T on X. Let ρ:H⁰(T,N_T/X)→H¹(T,T_T) be the connecting map of 0→T_T→T_X|_T→N_T/X→0, and let λ∈H¹(T,Ω¹_T) be the class of C in Hodge cohomology, the first Chern class of O_T(C) defined through its Atiyah class. Then for every n∈H⁰(T,N_T/X), ρ(n)∪λ=δ_div(δ_norm(n|_C)) in H²(T,O_T), where δ_norm:H⁰(C,N_T/X|_C)→H¹(C,N_C/T) is the connecting map of 0→N_C/T→N_C/X→N_T/X|_C→0 and δ_div:H¹(C,N_C/T)→H²(T,O_T) is that of 0→O_T→O_T(C)→O_T(C)|_C→0, with O_T(C)|_C≅N_C/T. For a family of surfaces in X through T with base B, the Kodaira–Spencer map at T is ρ∘k, where k:T_bB→H⁰(T,N_T/X) classifies the first-order embedded deformations; hence φ_λ=δ_div∘δ_norm∘res_C∘k.
hypotheses: C, T and X are smooth and projective over C, of dimensions 1, 2 and 3, with C⊂T⊂X.
The Chern class and the boundary signs use the same generator of Z(1) and the cup ordering of kodaira-spencer-contraction.

The identity is a statement about coherent cohomology. The source introduces λ as the image of the Betti class of C in H²(T(C),Z(1)); that this is the coherent Chern class is the comparison of first Chern classes under the de Rham–Betti isomorphism, needed only when the factorization is fed to the Griffiths formula, and is part of G1.
proofSteps: Compute connecting maps by extension cocycles formed from differences of local splittings; a connecting map is cup product with the extension class.

Pull the divisor extension back along T_T→N_C/T (extended by zero from C): the resulting extension of T_T by O_T has class λ. The source proves this by twisting by O_T(−C) and identifying the result with the dual of Atiyah's extension, whose class is −λ; dualizing changes the sign once.
The map of normal sequences from (T_T, T_X|_T, N_T/X) to (N_C/T, N_C/X, N_T/X|_C) and the pull-back diagram give the compatibility of the two connecting maps, hence the identity.
For a family, compose with the characteristic map: the Kodaira–Spencer map of a family of hypersurfaces is the characteristic map followed by ρ (B19 quotes Sernesi, Proposition 3.2.9(i), for this).
Use the degree-one group H¹(C,N_C/T) in the middle; B19 (5.7) prints degree zero there (source issue E-H8-1).

sources.match: The full extension-class argument proves the equality of the normal-boundary composite and contraction.
The factorization is applied to the family of double covers, after describing its Kodaira–Spencer map through the characteristic map; (5.7) has the degree misprint recorded as E-H8-1.

acceptance: The middle cohomology group is H¹(C,N_C/T); replacing it by H⁰ is ill-typed.

nodes.title: Generic vanishing criterion for divisor contraction
nodes.statement: In normal-boundary-factorization, if H¹(T,N_T/X(-C))=0, H¹(C,N_C/X)=0 and H²(T,O_T(C))=0, then φ_λ:H⁰(T,N_T/X)→H²(T,O_T) is surjective. For a family with characteristic map k:T_bB→H⁰(T,N_T/X), the conclusion on T_bB additionally requires k to be surjective, or that the composite restriction from T_bB to H⁰(C,N_T/X|_C) be surjective.
hypotheses: The three explicit vanishing hypotheses; a family parameter must supply the extra characteristic-map condition.
proofSteps: The restriction exact sequence gives surjectivity to H⁰(C,N_T/X|_C).
The normal cohomology sequence gives surjectivity of δ_norm.
The divisor cohomology sequence gives surjectivity of δ_div; compose using normal-boundary-factorization.

sources.match: The three stated vanishings force every map in the normal-boundary composite to be onto.

acceptance: Vanishing alone does not imply surjectivity for an arbitrary smaller parameter family.

nodes.title: Positive open cones of classes
nodes.statement: A positive open cone Ω in a finite-dimensional real vector space V is a nonempty open subset closed under multiplication by every positive real scalar. It need not be convex or closed under addition, and zero is permitted. Its topology is that of V, or explicitly of a kernel/fixed subspace when that is the ambient space.
hypotheses: V is a finite-dimensional normed real vector space; relative openness is stated in the actual target subspace.
proofSteps: Use a set with openness, nonemptiness and positive-scaling stability.
For positive a, stability for a and a⁻¹ gives aΩ=Ω.
A linear equivalence transports the set and all three properties.

sources.match: Positive scaling of the fibrewise linear evaluation map expands its open image into a nonempty open cone.
The cone is open in the pushforward kernel, not necessarily in all cohomology.

acceptance: The zero-dimensional target has the cone {0}; neither excluding zero nor demanding convexity is justified.

uses.how: A lattice-coset approximation is made in precisely the real subspace in which the cone is open.

nodes.title: Green’s evaluation submersion criterion
nodes.statement: Let H be a finite-rank effective real weight-two VHS on a complex manifold and choose a flat trivializing neighbourhood Δ of b. The smooth real bundle J of real (1,1)-classes has evaluation E:J→H_R,b by flat transport. If λ∈J_b and θ_λ:T_bB→H_b^(0,2) is onto as a complex-linear map, E is a submersion at (b,λ). The same statement holds for a rational subvariation, with its own Hodge pieces and target.
hypotheses: The local system, differentiable Hodge bundle, flat marking and Griffiths symbol are those of the common variation supplier.
Surjectivity is onto the (0,2) piece of the chosen variation, not onto the full ambient cohomology.
proofSteps: The fibre derivative contributes J_b.
The derivative normal to J_b is the real form of θ_λ and its conjugate; a real tangent vector of the complex base has arbitrary (1,0) component.
Complex surjectivity onto H^(0,2) therefore gives real surjectivity modulo J_b.
A submersion has open image near the point: Mathlib's map_nhds_eq_of_surj gives this directly in complete normed spaces; the implicit-function chart is the same statement with a straightening.

sources.match: Under the surjectivity hypothesis the evaluation from the real (1,1) bundle to the fixed real fibre is submersive at (b,λ); the source quotes Voisin's book for this.

sources.locator: Lemma 2 and the proof of Proposition 1, §1, author PDF pp.4–5; Proposition 8 proof, §3, p.20
sources.match: Lemma 2 states the equivalence between surjectivity of the contraction and submersivity of the evaluation on F¹; the proof of Proposition 1 passes to the real (1,1) bundle, and Proposition 8 repeats the argument for the push-forward kernel.

acceptance: A constant VHS with nonzero (0,2) piece cannot satisfy the hypothesis.

nodes.title: Surjectivity on real fixed tangent spaces
nodes.statement: Let s:E→E and t:F→F be real-linear involutions, and L:E→F an equivariant surjective real-linear map. The restriction L:E^s→F^t is onto. This remains true after changing both actions by the Tate sign. It is the linear input to restricting an equivariant submersion to smooth fixed loci.
hypotheses: Scalar field R, so2 is invertible.
L∘s=t∘L; both actions are involutive.
proofSteps: For y fixed by t choose x with Lx=y.
The averaged vector (x+s(x))/2 is fixed by s and still maps to y.
Apply the argument to the actual tangent actions; nonlinear fixed-locus charts need the separate manifold supplier.

sources.match: Tangent invariants of the two fixed loci retain surjectivity of the equivariant derivative.

acceptance: In characteristic2 this averaging proof and general conclusion fail; the theorem is specifically real-linear.

nodes.title: Real Green open-cone theorem
nodes.statement: Let H be an effective rational weight-two VHS on B(C), for a smooth algebraic variety B over R, with a compatible real action; let b∈B(R) and λ∈H_R,b^(1,1)(1)^G, and suppose θ_λ:T_bB(C)→H_b^(0,2) is surjective. Let Δ be any G-stable connected analytic neighbourhood of b in B(C) on which the local system is trivial and whose real locus Δ(R)=Δ∩B(R) is connected and contractible. Then there is a positive open cone Ω⊂H_R,b(1)^G such that every ν∈Ω, transported flatly over Δ, lies in H_R,b′^(1,1)(1)^G for some b′∈Δ(R): it is of type (1,1) there and is still twisted-invariant, because the marking of a G-stable chart is G-equivariant. Openness is relative to H_R,b(1)^G. Such neighbourhoods exist inside every neighbourhood of b, so Δ may be taken arbitrarily small; the cone depends on Δ.
hypotheses: B is a smooth algebraic variety over R, so B(R) is the fixed locus of an antiholomorphic involution of the complex manifold B(C); the fixed Hodge bundle is a manifold whose tangent spaces are the fixed tangent spaces (the fixed-locus theorem of G3).
λ has the Tate sign and is real of type (1,1); θ_λ is onto the complex (0,2) target.
Δ is admissible in the sense of the statement; no smallness is needed beyond that.
proofSteps: Apply green-evaluation-submersion to the evaluation on the real (1,1) bundle over Δ; it is G-equivariant because the trivialization of a connected G-stable chart is unique.

Twist by Z(1) and pass to G-invariants: by the fixed-locus theorem and fixed-linear-surjectivity the restricted evaluation from the twisted-invariant (1,1) bundle over Δ(R) to H_R,b(1)^G is a submersion at (b,λ).
Its image therefore contains a neighbourhood of λ in H_R,b(1)^G (map_nhds_eq_of_surj in charts).
The image is stable under positive scaling because evaluation is fibrewise linear; the positive saturation of that neighbourhood is the cone, and it contains λ.

sources.match: For the neighbourhood chosen at the start of §1.2 the proposition gives an open cone in the twisted-invariant real fibre whose elements are, after the trivialization, twisted-invariant classes of type (1,1) at points of the real locus of the neighbourhood.
This criterion is invoked on the vanishing variation in the real-surface application.

acceptance: Neither existence of real basepoints nor complex Noether–Lefschetz density supplies the rank hypothesis.

In a supplied chart this predicate uses an actual real submodule J_b and the real-linear class-to-symbol map J_b→Hom_C(T_bB,H_b^(0,2)); it is not existence of any Hodge class.
hypotheses: Finite-dimensional Hodge pieces; the derivative family is the actual Griffiths symbol.
Real-analyticity is required for the density theorem, not built into this set definition.
proofSteps: Quantify over the twisted real (1,1) subspace.
Express onto by the native linear-map range condition.
The zero target is handled without assuming a nonzero class exists.

nodes.title: Componentwise density of the real criterion
nodes.statement: For a finite-rank weight-two compatible real VHS over the complex points of a smooth real algebraic variety, Good_R(H) is open, and on each connected component K of B(R) it is either empty or open dense. In particular one good point in K implies density in that K. For a geometric smooth projective real family the condition is equivalently surjectivity of KS contraction on an invariant twisted (1,1)-class.
hypotheses: The fixed Hodge bundle and derivative family have real-analytic local frames; fibre dimensions are locally constant.
Connected components are those of the smooth real manifold B(R).
Openness of the good locus is not in the source's statement; it follows from its proof, which shows that the complement is a closed real-analytic subset.
proofSteps: In local frames expand maximal-rank minors as finite homogeneous polynomials in the class coordinates.
Badness at a basepoint means every coefficient of every such minor vanishes: this is a finite system of real-analytic equations, not an unproved arbitrary intersection assertion.
If badness contains a nonempty open set, the several-variable analytic identity principle propagates vanishing along the connected component.
Otherwise the closed bad set has empty interior; goodness is open dense. Use griffiths-derivative for the geometric formulation.

sources.locator: Proposition 1.2 and its proof, §1.3, p.1051; Proposition 1.3, §1.4, p.1052
sources.match: The real-analytic rank condition has the componentwise empty-or-dense alternative; the next proposition identifies the geometric criterion.
Complex density alone does not force the real criterion locus to be nonempty.

nodes.title: Constant and vanishing weight-two summands
nodes.statement: Suppose an effective rational weight-two VHS has a flat rational symmetric bilinear pairing Q and a constant Hodge sub-local-system C with fixed Hodge filtration, such that Q restricted to C is nondegenerate and Q_C(H^(p,q),H^(r,s))=0 unless p+r=q+s=2. Then K=C^⊥ is a flat rational Hodge subvariation, H=C⊕K and the projector to C is flat and a Hodge morphism. A compatible real action preserving C and Q preserves K. In surface-cover applications Q is the full intersection pairing; it is not asserted to be a polarization of all H² without the Lefschetz sign correction.
hypotheses: Q is flat and nondegenerate on C; C is a subvariation with constant Hodge filtration.
Q is a Hodge pairing of total type(2,2), with the stated vanishing between unmatched Hodge types.
proofSteps: Fibrewise, Mathlib's isCompl_orthogonal_of_restrict_nondegenerate gives H_b=C_b⊕C_b^⊥ from nondegeneracy of Q on C_b alone (Q symmetric, the fibre finite-dimensional). When Q is a polarization this agrees with the native Tau Ceti complement theorem, which is the polarized special case.
Flatness of Q and C makes the fibre orthogonal spaces locally constant under parallel transport.
Hodge-type orthogonality splits each piece and the filtration; nondegeneracy on C produces the direct sum.
Preservation of the two inputs by real action gives preservation of K.

sources.match: The weight-two variation decomposes as the constant cohomology of the base surface and its cup-product orthogonal vanishing subvariation.

acceptance: For a degree-d surface map, p_*p^*=d on rational cohomology gives the normalized projector d⁻¹p^*p_* and identifies K with ker p_*.

nodes.title: No derivative into a constant Hodge summand
nodes.statement: For the flat Hodge splitting H=C⊕K with C having constant Hodge filtration, the period symbol respects the splitting and its C-part vanishes: θ_b(v) is zero on C_b^(1,1) and maps K_b^(1,1) into K_b^(0,2). Hence, writing λ=λ_C+λ_K for λ∈H_b^(1,1), θ_λ=θ_(λ_K), and θ_λ(T_bB) lies in K_b^(0,2).
hypotheses: Use the flat Hodge projector of orthogonal-constant-splitting.
proofSteps: A parallel C-section remains in the same filtration step, so its Gauss–Manin symbol is zero.
Naturality of the symbol under the flat projector kills the C-projection of θ_λ.

sources.match: The derivative has image in the vanishing part, because the other summand is constant.

acceptance: Constancy of the underlying local system alone is insufficient; the Hodge filtration of C must also be constant.

nodes.title: Codimension criterion on the vanishing summand
nodes.statement: Let H_b^(0,2)=C_b^(0,2)⊕K_b^(0,2), and f:T_bB→H_b^(0,2) have image in K_b^(0,2). If codim_(H^(0,2))(im f)≤dim_C C_b^(0,2), then f, with codomain restricted to K_b^(0,2), is surjective. The inequality is equivalent to equality because the image containment gives the reverse bound.
hypotheses: Finite-dimensional complex vector spaces; the actual image-containment and direct-sum identification are supplied.
proofSteps: Write dim H=dim C+dim K and codim(im f)=dim C+dim K-dim(im f).
The stated inequality gives dim(im f)≥dim K; containment gives the reverse inequality.
Equal dimensions and containment force equality of subspaces.

nodes.title: Real Green criterion for the vanishing variation
nodes.statement: Under orthogonal-constant-splitting with a compatible real action preserving C and Q, let b be real and let λ∈H_R,b^(1,1)(1)^G be a twisted-invariant real (1,1)-class of the ambient variation; in the source it is the class of a real curve, which does not lie in K. If the cokernel of its geometric contraction φ_λ:T_bB(C)→H_b^(0,2) has dimension at most dim_C C_b^(0,2), then for every admissible neighbourhood Δ of b as in real-green-open-cone, now trivializing K, there is a positive open cone in K_R,b(1)^G whose classes, transported over Δ, are twisted-invariant classes of K of type (1,1) at points of Δ(R). The cone is open in the vanishing twisted-invariant subspace.
hypotheses: The constant summand has constant Hodge filtration, and the splitting is compatible with the real action.

λ is any twisted-invariant real (1,1)-class of H at b; the theorem is applied to its K-component λ_K, which is again real, of type (1,1) and twisted-invariant because the Hodge projector is rational, flat and commutes with the real action.
All geometric comparison suppliers of griffiths-derivative are supplied.
proofSteps: Compare the contraction with the period symbol by griffiths-derivative.
By constant-symbol-zero, θ_λ=θ_(λ_K) and its image lies in K_b^(0,2); by vanishing-rank-criterion it is onto K_b^(0,2).
Apply real-green-open-cone to the subvariation K and the class λ_K.

sources.match: The class of the curve is a twisted-invariant real (1,1)-class of the whole variation; its derivative has cokernel of dimension at most h²(O_S) and image in the vanishing part, hence is onto the vanishing (0,2)-piece, and the real criterion is then applied to the vanishing variation.

acceptance: The application does not replace the ambient rank estimate by a hypothesis of surjectivity onto all H²(O).

nodes.title: Full lattice cosets meet positive open cones
nodes.statement: Let V be a finite-dimensional normed real space, b a finite real basis, Λ=span_Z(range b), n a positive integer, a∈V and Ω a positive open cone in V. Then (a+nΛ)∩Ω is nonempty. Thus the result applies to every full-rank finite-index sublattice and every coset in its real span; it does not apply to a lower-rank lattice in a larger ambient space.
hypotheses: n>0; openness and nonemptiness hold in the same full real span as the lattice.
No rationality of the cone or of a is needed.
proofSteps: Choose v∈Ω and a ball of radius ε>0 around v contained in Ω.
For large t>0 choose z=floor_b((t v-a)/n); native norm_fract_le bounds ||a+nz-tv|| by n times the sum of basis norms.
After dividing by t the error tends to zero, so (a+nz)/t belongs to the chosen ball.
Positive-scaling stability gives a+nz∈Ω; dimension zero is automatic.

sources.locator: Proposition1.2 proof, p.71; Proposition6.6 proof, p.94
sources.match: A prescribed coset of a full lattice meets the open cone; the real proof uses the same elementary approximation.

acceptance: The positive real ray meets every congruence class a+nZ for n>0.
For Λ=Z×{0} in R², a cone disjoint from that axis demonstrates why full rank matters.

nodes.title: Voisin’s high-degree kernel rank theorem
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth projective complex threefold with a morphism p:X→S to a smooth projective surface, whose generic fibre is a smooth rational curve. Choose an ample line bundle H with H²·K_X<0; replacing H by a sufficiently high positive power provides the very-ampleness and positive-twist cohomology hypotheses used in the proof. For all sufficiently large m and a general smooth T∈|mH|, there is λ∈ker[p_*:H¹(T,Ω¹_T)→H¹(S,Ω¹_S)] for which φ_λ:H⁰(T,N_T/X)→ker[p_*:H²(T,O_T)→H²(S,O_S)] is surjective.
hypotheses: p is a morphism with rational generic fibre; X,S smooth projective over C.
The negative canonical intersection hypothesis and all sufficiently-large-degree bounds in Voisin’s proof are retained.
proofSteps: Use the bilinear cup pairing and Serre duality to reduce generic surjectivity to absence of oversized components of its projective base locus (Voisin Lemma6).

Degenerate to determinantal nodal surfaces; the limiting pairing includes products of evaluations at the nodes (Lemma7). Barth’s node count, Grassmannian Koszul/Bott vanishing and uniform position give the O(m²) projection/rank bound.

The generic low-rank loci have dimension bounded independently of m (Proposition5, projection to P³ and Fermat Jacobian-ring count). Green’s linear-series growth estimate then rules out bounded nonzero ranks (Propositions6–7).

In the kernel setting, the natural pushforward identifies H³(X,Ω¹_X) with H²(S,O_S), so the surface pushforward kernel equals the Gysin kernel. Residues span this kernel on H²(O_T); the annihilator under Serre duality is p^*H⁰(S,K_S), disjoint from its kernel by the pull-push degree identity. This is the modification in Proposition9.
These general proof suppliers have explicit requests and gaps; no unresolved cited estimate is described as a native library theorem.

sources.locator: Proposition9, §3 author PDF p.21; full support: Lemmas6–10, Propositions3–7, §2 pp.8–18 and Appendix pp.22–23
sources.match: The high-degree kernel contraction is onto, using the listed general nodal, rank, linear-series and residue arguments.
The required kernel infinitesimal criterion is the Voisin result that produces the complex cone.

acceptance: When H²(O_S) is nonzero, the target remains the kernel; no full-target surjectivity is claimed.

nodes.title: Voisin’s pushforward-kernel open cone
nodes.statement: Under voisin-infinitesimal-kernel, for all sufficiently large m there is a nonempty Zariski open V in the smooth-divisor parameter space |mH| such that for every b∈V(C) and every connected contractible neighbourhood Δ of b in V(C), some positive open cone Ω⊂ker[p_*:H²(T_b,R)→H²(S,R)] consists of classes which become type(1,1) on a fibre over Δ. This is a complex deformation theorem: the points realizing the classes are in Δ(C), and no real-locus conclusion is included.
hypotheses: The pushforward is a flat Hodge map in the universal divisor family; its kernel is a common-carrier weight-two subvariation.
Voisin’s general high-degree hypothesis and the kernel rank theorem are supplied.
proofSteps: Flat pushforward defines the kernel local system, with constant rank and induced Hodge filtration.

The infinitesimal theorem holds on a nonempty open rank locus; existence of some λ is an algebraic open condition by maximal minors in local frames.

nodes.title: Andreotti–Frankel affine CW bound
nodes.statement: Every smooth complex affine variety of complex dimension d has the homotopy type of a CW complex of real dimension at most d. In particular a smooth affine complex surface has CW dimension at most2. The statement is ordinary topology; a finite étale cover is another affine variety and must have the theorem applied to it separately.
hypotheses: Smooth affine of pure complex dimension d; singular affine varieties require a different theorem.
proofSteps: Embed the affine variety as a closed complex submanifold M of C^N.

For almost every point p the squared distance from p, restricted to M, has only nondegenerate critical points. In a chart of M formed by 2d of the real ambient coordinates it is a fixed function minus an inner-product term in the chart coordinates, so Tau Ceti's genericity theorem for inner-product perturbations applies chart by chart; countably many charts give almost every p. The function is proper and bounded below because M is closed.

At a critical point the native Morse index, read in a chart through its invariance under changes of coordinates, is at most d: in a normal direction the second fundamental form of a complex submanifold is the real part of a holomorphic quadratic form, whose eigenvalues occur in opposite pairs, so at most d of the 2d Hessian eigenvalues are negative (Milnor, §7, Assertions 1 and 2).

The handle theorem for a nondegenerate function with compact sublevel sets (Milnor, Theorem 3.5) gives a CW model with one cell of dimension the index for each critical point. That theorem is stated by no roadmap and is gap G3. Nondegenerate critical points, the Morse index and generic Morse perturbations are already in Tau Ceti at the pin, on normed spaces; their manifold-level form belongs to the Morse homology lane of the upstream Heegaard Floer roadmap, for which they were built.

Poincaré duality identifies these homology groups with H³(T,Z), H⁵(X,Z), and identifies inclusion with Gysin.
